content:
maya: Quick heads-up — noticed a p99 spike on cluster-a overnight around 02:13 UTC. p50 looks stable but p99 doubled for short prompts (<=64 tokens).
liam: any traces or flamegraphs?
maya: attaching quick summary — throughput up ~18% at the time, but tail shot up from ~780ms to ~1.6s. link: https://perf.internal/runs/2026-03-17/173999
anya: I pulled scheduler and kv metrics for that window. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~92% -> ~71% for affected hosts.
kevin: that drop can force fallback to the slower kernel path (fast_small -> fallback_bf16). we saw similar p99 bumps when min_kv_hit_before_fast_kernel was crossed.
maya: current prod scheduler config (excerpt):

```yaml
max_batch_tokens: 4096
max_wait_ms: 8
max_batch_size: 64
microbatch_target_tokens: 64
min_kv_hit_for_fast_kernel: 0.85
kernel_pref_order: [fast_small, fallback_bf16, large_tile]
```

liam: so if KV hit goes <0.85 we pick fallback_bf16 which adds ~250-350ms per request for short sequences?
anya: exactly. I profiled the worst traces: fallback kernel execution + extra mem copies ~320ms median on those tails. plus queuing jitter. snippet from trace: 

```
TRACE: request=0x8a3f
queue_wait_ms=12
kernel_choice=fallback_bf16
exec_ms=328
kv_miss_count=4
```

kevin: interestingly, queue_wait_ms spiked too (from 4ms -> ~12ms). I think continuous-batching behavior combined with kernel fallback caused a positive feedback — slower exec -> longer queue -> more microbatches hitting kv misses as cache evictions align.
maya: hypothesis: interplay between max_batch_tokens and max_wait_ms creates a zone where low KV hit amplifies tail. need to test two levers: reduce max_batch_tokens (so fewer tokens per batch) OR lower max_wait_ms to reduce queuing at cost of throughput. also consider raising min_kv_hit_for_fast_kernel (to force different routing) or add a guarded fast-path that tolerates occasional kv misses.
liam: propose short experiment matrix (canary on 3 hosts):
- A: max_wait_ms=4, max_batch_tokens=2048
- B: max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096, min_kv_hit_for_fast_kernel=0.80
- C: max_wait_ms=2, max_batch_tokens=1024, microbatch_target_tokens=32

anya: I ran a small offline replay for A/B/C with synthetic traffic (same latency distribution). results (p99 short prompt):
- baseline: 1.6s
- A: 930ms (throughput -6%)
- B: 1.1s (throughput -2%)
- C: 820ms (throughput -12%)

kevin: C looks best for tail but biggest throughput loss. A is a good middle ground. B reduces tail but less throughput impact.
liam: what about kernel-routing change? if we allow fast_small to handle some kv-miss cases (maybe gapped fallback) we could avoid full penalty. but risk correctness/perf regression for certain models.
maya: agree — gating kernel-routing change needs model-level validation. For now lean on scheduler params.
anya: also saw increased variance when microbatch_target_tokens=64 + max_wait_ms=8 — microburst arrival leads to microbatch coalescing that collides with KV eviction windows. shrinking microbatch_target_tokens to 32 smooths that.
kevin: actionable plan:
1) Canary A (max_wait_ms=4, max_batch_tokens=2048, microbatch_target_tokens=48) on 3 hosts for 2 hours. monitor p50/p95/p99 + KV hit + qps.
2) If A reduces p99 by >=30% and qps drop <=10% roll to 20% cluster.
3) Parallel safety experiment B (min_kv_hit tweak) in staging with eval harness.
4) Start a profiling capture for any host hitting p99 > 1s after rollout.

maya: I'll schedule canary and add dashboard widgets (p99 by short/long prompt buckets).
liam: I'll prepare the replay to validate A under heavier QPS.
anya: I'll add an alert rule: if after canary cluster p99 > 1.2s trigger auto-rollback.
kevin: noting: if we see queue_wait_ms > 20ms consistently we should pause rollout and dig deeper.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for config A scheduled at 2026-03-18T09:15:00Z -> hosts: cluster-a-03, cluster-a-04, cluster-a-07. monitor link: https://infra/rollouts/1739990210-canary
maya: thanks — will check in 30m after start. :eyes: 
liam: will post replay results and updated flamegraphs in this thread.
anya: added logs hook to gather full kernel traces for any p99 incidents.
kevin: remembering to capture KV eviction timeline (redis metrics) — that will help correlate.
maya: cool. if we get consistent improvement we should add a permanent tuning doc for "latency-throughput lattice" (scheduling knobs + kv interactions).
